questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question explores end-to-end data pipelines and production fault tolerance—a gap in many existing interview questions that focus primarily on REST-like paths or intermittent services. It tests a candidate's understanding of orchestration, data integrity, and chaos resilience in distributed streaming systems.

## Key Concepts

- End-to-end testing for data pipelines
- Exactly-once semantics with idempotent sinks and transactional offsets
- Late-arriving data handling with watermarking
- Chaos testing and fault injection
- Observability and reproducible datasets

## Testing Strategy

| Test Type | Dataset | Success Criteria |
|-----------|---------|-------------------|
| Correctness | 100K synthetic records with known schema | All records correctly transformed and stored in PostgreSQL with matching values |
| Latency | Timed event batches injected at source | End-to-end latency < 5 seconds at 99th percentile |
| Exactly-Once | Duplicate producer records with same transaction IDs | No duplicate rows in sink; exactly one instance of each event |
| Late-Arriving Data | Out-of-order events with timestamps up to 10 minutes old | Watermarked events processed correctly; no premature eviction |
| Broker Restart | Kill -9 simulation mid-stream | Zero data loss; processing resumes from last checkpoint |
| Topic Compaction Pause | Suspended compaction during active ingestion | No data loss after compaction resumes |
| Partial Deploy | Rolling restart of Spark executors | Zero duplication; exactly-once semantics maintained |

## Success Criteria Summary

- All test types must pass without manual intervention
- CI pipeline completes in under 30 minutes
- Reproducible results across multiple test runs
- Zero false positives in failure scenario detection

```python
def reconcile_event(event_id, mongo_doc, oracle_row):

    return hash(str(mongo_doc)) == hash(str(oracle_row)) and event_id == oracle_row["id"]
```
